name: High and tight

card.summary: A military haircut with very short sides and back and a short top, giving a clean, defined head shape that is easy to maintain.

quick.overview:
The high and tight is a short military haircut in which the back and sides are clipped very close up to a point above the temples, with a slightly longer top. The sharp line between the lengths emphasizes head shape and jaw.

It began in the US armed forces and spread to civilian wear in the late 1980s. Many wearers also choose short cuts for low maintenance and for thinning hair.
quick.how: Barbers clip the sides and back to 1.6 mm or less up to above the temples and leave the top around 5 to 10 mm, per Wikipedia. Variations include the horseshoe flattop and the recon.
quick.risks: There are no health risks beyond ordinary clipper irritation or sun exposure on a shorn scalp. Results depend on head shape and hairline.

lead: The high and tight is a military variant of the crew cut. The back and sides are clipped very short, usually 1.6 mm or less, to a point above the temples, while the top is about 5 to 10 mm, with a sharp line between them [1].

Wearers use it for a clean, defined outline and low maintenance. Wikipedia reports the crown is shaved less closely so a combat helmet fits [1]. Its civilian spread began in the late 1980s, first among young Black men, where it is linked to the hi-top fade [1].

Variations are the horseshoe flattop, which leaves the scalp centre visible, and the recon, which starts hair high above the crown [1]. A broader article on the buzz cut notes short cuts are often chosen by people with thinning hairlines and can make the face look more defined [2].

chain: Very short sides with a sharp contrast line
angle.text: The tight sides remove volume around the face so the jaw and skull shape read clearly. It is also used to manage thinning hair.

paras: A sharp line separates the short sides from the longer top, and the crown is cut less closely for helmet fit [1].

Common in the US armed forces and among law enforcement, it entered civilian life in the late 1980s, and from the 1990s has been popular with youths in several countries; in Indonesia it is called Cepak and is worn by military personnel [1]. Short buzz cuts in general began as a measure against head lice and persist for ease of maintenance, cooling and uniformity [2].
